name: insrc_analyze
title: insrc analyze
description:
One-shot analyze: runs the full insrc pipeline server-side and returns a verified, citation-grounded 7-layer bundle (system, focus, summary, structure, surface, artefacts, upstream) in a single tool call. Prefer this variant for STRUCTURAL-MAP questions (module maps, tree layout, entity counts) where no narrow-LLM reasoning is needed; inner LLM calls (if any) go to the daemon's configured shaperProvider (Ollama by default).

For adherence-check, capability-discovery, or prose-retrieval intents, prefer the sibling tool `insrc_analyze_step` -- it hands narrow-LLM reasoning to YOUR model in-session (better accuracy, no subprocess spawns, no separate billing).

Read the user's prompt yourself and send a structured `request`: the `question`, the `scopeRef` it names (a module or file path, a symbol, a repo) and any `context`. Send `focus` alone only for a question about the whole workspace.

Prefer either analyze tool over Read/Grep/Glob for:
  - "map / explore <module>"
  - "does the codebase already do <X>?"
  - "how does <Y> work?"
  - "does the code follow <rule> from <doc>?"
  - "what conventions does <module> follow?"
  - "list every registered <data source | infra manifest>"
  - Any question a text match alone would answer wrongly or incompletely.

Use Read/Grep/Glob instead when a text match alone answers it ("where does this text occur?", "show me this function"). Call again with a narrower `request` to drill down. Fall back to Read/Grep/Glob also when the tool returns an empty or clearly off-topic bundle.

repo.description: Absolute path (or registered repo name) the analyze framework should operate on. Must match a repo previously registered via `insrc repo add`. If unset, the daemon's default repo (from `INSRC_REPO` env / config) is used; when neither is set, the call fails with a repo-not-found error listing every registered repo.

focus.description: Prompt-only fallback: one-line natural-language framing of what to analyze, run over the whole workspace. E.g. "map the payable extraction module", "does the CLAUDE.md Haiku rule hold?", or "list every registered data source". The framework's classifier turns this into a structured intent + picks a deterministic recipe.

request.description: Preferred over `focus`: the structured request built from the user's prompt (question, scopeRef, optional target, sizeHint, context). Send `request` or `focus`, not both with different text; `target` and `scope` are ignored when `request` is sent.

question.description: What to answer, in the user's words or tightened by you. Not the whole conversation.

value.description: An absolute path for module / file / manifest-dir; for a symbol, `<absolute file path>#<entity name>` (a bare name is not accepted); a connection name; or the repo path.

scopeRef.description: What to analyse. Decide it from the prompt; use `workspace` only when the prompt names no area.

target.description: Optional target hint; defaults to code.

sizeHint.description: Optional. The size you expect; a hint only, as the size is measured.

context.description: Optional background the user gave that bears on the answer (at most 4000 characters). It never decides the scope.

target.description: Optional target hint. Skip the classifier's target inference when the caller already knows.

scope.description: Optional. The size you expect the request to be (XS smallest, XL largest). It is a hint only: the size is measured from what the request touches, and the answer reports both.

name: insrc_analyze_step
title: insrc analyze (multi-turn)
description:
Phase-driven multi-turn context analyzer. Alternative to `insrc_analyze` for clients that want to keep every LLM reasoning turn in-session (no subprocess spawn, no MCP sampling required). Use when:

  - The user asks about a repository's code structure, conventions, adherence, reuse candidates, or design decisions.
  - A text match alone would give a wrong or incomplete answer.

Use Read/Grep/Glob instead when a text match alone answers it ("where does this text occur?", "show me this function").

Multi-turn loop:

  1. Call phase='start' with a `request` built from the user's prompt
     (question + scopeRef), or `focus` alone for a whole-workspace
     question. Server returns
     { next: 'emit_plan', prompt, schema, state }.
  2. Follow the prompt to emit a JSON object matching the schema
     (the ExplorationPlan). Then call phase='plan' with your
     plan + state.
  3. If the server returns { next: 'emit_narrow', prompt, schema,
     state, explorationId }, emit the JSON matching the schema and
     call phase='narrow' with your JSON + explorationId + state.
     Repeat until the server returns emit_bundle instead.
  4. Server returns { next: 'emit_bundle', prompt, schema, state }.
     Emit the bundle JSON, then call phase='bundle' with your
     bundle + state.
  5. Server returns { next: 'done', markdown } -- render this
     to the user.

The `guidance` field on each response explains what to do next in one sentence; the `prompt` + `schema` fields are the authoritative instructions. Preserve `state` verbatim between calls.

phase.description: Which turn of the loop this call carries. Start a new run with `start`, then walk through `plan` -> optional `narrow` (one or more) -> `bundle`. The `narrow` phase is ONLY needed when the prior response was next="emit_narrow"; the server tells you which via the `next` field.

focus.description: Only for phase=start. Prompt-only fallback: natural-language framing of what to analyze, over the whole workspace. Prefer `request`.

request.description: Only for phase=start. Preferred over `focus`: the structured request built from the user's prompt (question, scopeRef, optional target, sizeHint, context). `target` and `scope` are ignored when it is sent.

question.description: What to answer, in the user's words or tightened by you. Not the whole conversation.

value.description: An absolute path for module / file / manifest-dir; for a symbol, `<absolute file path>#<entity name>` (a bare name is not accepted); a connection name; or the repo path.

scopeRef.description: What to analyse. Decide it from the prompt; use `workspace` only when the prompt names no area.

target.description: Optional target hint; defaults to code.

sizeHint.description: Optional. The size you expect; a hint only, as the size is measured.

context.description: Optional background the user gave that bears on the answer (at most 4000 characters). It never decides the scope.

repo.description: Only for phase=start. Absolute repo path; falls back to INSRC_REPO env.

target.description: Only for phase=start. Optional target hint.

scope.description: Only for phase=start. Optional. The size you expect the request to be; a hint only, as the size is measured.

plan.description: Only for phase=plan. The ExplorationPlan JSON your LLM emitted from the prior emit_plan response.

narrow.description: Only for phase=narrow. The JSON your LLM emitted matching the schema from the prior emit_narrow response (finalizes one narrow-LLM exploration).

explorationId.description: Only for phase=narrow. Echo the explorationId from the prior emit_narrow response so the server can cross-check which exploration this narrow output finalizes.

bundle.description: Only for phase=bundle. The AnalyzeContextBundle JSON your LLM emitted from the prior emit_bundle response.

state.description: Opaque continuation token from the prior tool response. Required for phase='plan' and phase='bundle'; server generates it on phase='start'.

name: insrc_build_step
title: insrc build (controller-driven)
description:
Lean, controller-driven build surface for implementing ONE approved plan Task. The daemon resolves + gates + templatizes; YOU (the controller) do the editing. Stateless — each call is self-contained given `target` (a task id: `#N`, a hierarchical id, or `s1/t3`).

Phases:

  - `implement` — { target }. The daemon runs the admission gate (plan present + approved + fresh) and returns one of:
      { next: "refused", refusal }            — plan missing/unapproved/stale;
      { next: "implement", taskId, workflowId, issueRef, prompt } — EXECUTE the returned prompt: edit code, run tests, commit. The daemon did NOT edit. The prompt surfaces any design decisions resolved at plan-start (from the Story LLD's meta.questionResolutions). Open questions are resolved at stage STARTS via insrc_workflow_step, not here.

  - `validate` — { target, tests? }. The DAEMON runs the typecheck and the Task's tests itself, then a read-only verdict session against the repo, and returns { next: "done", verdict, passed }. `passed` is the daemon's judgment, never a self-report. Pass `tests` to say which test cases (a file and a test title) carry each test the Task names: the daemon runs those files, records a result per case in the Story's test record (TESTS.md beside BUILD.md), and fails the Task when a case fails, is skipped or is not found. A wrong mapping returns the error `invalid-test-mapping` and nothing is run.

`repo` is the absolute path of a registered repo (default: the registered repo that contains the session workspace, sent explicitly). The daemon refuses implement and validate when the repo is missing or not registered.

target.description: Task identifier: `#N`, `owner/repo#N`, a canonical/slug hierarchical id, or `s1/t3`. Ignored for a standalone (no-plan) build.

repo.description: Absolute path of a registered repo; defaults to the registered repo that contains the session workspace. The daemon refuses the call when it is missing or not registered.

epicHash.description: Optional epic scope for a structural `target` (`s1/t3`) when the repo holds more than one epic — a full or prefix DEF hash naming the epic. Ignored for issue# / hierarchical ids and single-epic dirs.
Standalone story identity (self-minted hash). Required for a Small build (locates the approved LLD).

storyId.description: Standalone story id; defaults to s1.

focus.description: Scope statement — the spec for a Trivial (no-LLD) build.

triageRationale.description: The classifier's rationale, stamped on the standalone BUILD record.

standalone.description: Present for a triage-routed no-plan build (Small implements the approved standalone LLD; Trivial implements the scope). Bypasses task/tracker resolution.

summary.description: Only for phase=validate. OPTIONAL narrative of what this build actually did, in a sentence or two — lands on the BUILD record's `body.summary` and renders as `## Summary`. Never synthesised: omit it and the record carries no summary rather than one invented from the task list. Empty / whitespace-only counts as omitted.

name.description: The exact text of one of the Task's named tests (for a standalone Small build: of a subject of the design's test strategy).

cases.description: The test cases that carry this named test.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the tracked `.test.ts` file.

title.description: The test's title exactly as the test file declares it; matched at any depth of nesting.

reported.description: Only for a `live` or `smoke` test the gate cannot run: the result you observed. Recorded as reported by the builder, not run by the gate.

evidence.description: Where the evidence is: a log path, a run id, a section of the build record.

tests.description: Only for phase=validate. The mapping from the Task's named tests to the test cases that carry them. The daemon runs each mapped file itself, reads a result per case (pass / fail / skipped / not found) and writes them to the Story's test record (TESTS.md beside BUILD.md); a case that failed, was skipped or was not found fails the tests check. Omit it to reuse the mapping stored for the Task by an earlier validate turn; with neither, only a test name that begins with `<file>.test.ts:` can be run. A wrong mapping is refused with `invalid-test-mapping` and nothing is run. Ignored for a Trivial standalone build.

name: insrc_code_review_step
title: Review committed task changes
description: Task-oriented code review by the party that did not write the code. Controller-authored code is reviewed by the daemon; daemon-authored code is reviewed by the live controller. No substitute self-review. Create a committed packet before start, with an explicit full-OID reviewRevision pin for final source; selected after-blocks/deletion anchors alone define scope and commits are provenance pointers. Start acknowledges in the background; poll progress/checkpoint, explicitly resume interrupted attempts. Controller reviewers return scope/activity/result on the live owner connection. No HEAD-derived scope, auto retries or retired engine.

reviewRevision.description: Required explicit full Git commit OID for the final reviewed source revision. All selected origin commits must be its ancestors. Never infer HEAD. Original commit selections remain provenance; only their verified final projections authorize findings.

testCoverage.description: Mandatory evidence-backed review of relevant test coverage. Verified means this assessment is complete, not that tests were executed. Report demonstrated coverage defects in findings.

limitations.description: Blocking omissions of mandatory code/module, requirements or test-coverage review only. Any skipped required review scope means incomplete. Do not put skipped optional execution here.

advice.description: Nonblocking optional execution disclosures (integration checks, tests, typecheck or build not run) and optional improvements. Prefix execution disclosures with Optional execution:.

name: insrc_docgen
title: insrc docgen (generate a self-contained code document)
description:
Generate a self-contained, offline HTML developer document from the indexed code graph (diagram inlined, zoom/pan, no network). Read-only; the graph is read INSIDE the daemon and only the finished document crosses back.

`docType` is a registered document type — e.g. type-structure (class/inheritance), component-dependency (module topology), call-sequence (a flow from an entry-point `symbol`), or narrative (a `base` diagram + an LLM answer to `question`). Enumerate the authoritative current set + each type's inputs via the daemon docgen.list surface rather than assuming this list.

Per-type scope fields: `path` (subtree), `symbol` (call-sequence entry point), `base` + `question` (narrative), `maxDepth` (traversal cap). `repo` falls back to the session workspace / INSRC_REPO and must be registered + finished indexing (else source-not-ready).

docType.description: Registered docgen document type (enumerate the current set via docgen.list).

repo.description: Absolute repo path; falls back to the session workspace / INSRC_REPO. Must be registered + indexed.

path.description: Repo-relative subtree to scope the document (type-structure / component-dependency).

base.description: Base diagram for a narrative doc: call-sequence | component-dependency.

question.description: The question a narrative document should answer (required for narrative).

name: insrc_guide
title: insrc guide (fetch one workflow's full guidance)
description:
Read-only: return the full step-by-step guidance for a specific insrc workflow, on demand, sourced from the canonical steering content the daemon ships (so it reflects the single source with no per-repo copy).

Call it BEFORE running a workflow whose detailed procedure you need, instead of relying on the injected skeleton. Omit / mistype `workflow` to get { error, validWorkflows } (a structured list, never thrown).

workflow.description: The workflow whose full step-by-step guidance you want (e.g. "design.story"). Omit it to receive the list of workflows that have authored guidance.

name: insrc_present
title: insrc present (declare the documents a turn shows for review)
description: Declare the documents you are asking the user to review, BEFORE you ask them to approve: the chat opens exactly the documents named here in its review pane. Pass one to twenty artifact ids (for example `LLD-<hash>-s1`) or repo-relative document paths. The answer lists which names are `presented` (pending approval and openable) and which are `notPending` (misspelt, already approved, with no document file yet, or a path that matches more than one document), so you can correct a mistake at once. Changes nothing and approves nothing. `repo` falls back to the session workspace / INSRC_REPO.

documents.description: One to twenty artifact ids or repo-relative document paths the user is asked to review.

repo.description: Absolute repo path; falls back to the session workspace / INSRC_REPO.

name: insrc_review_step
title: Review evolving design artifacts
description: Review DEF/HLD/LLD by the party that did not author it. Controller-authored artifacts go to the daemon; daemon-authored artifacts go to the live controller. Start acknowledges durable background work; poll progress, retrieve one completed chunk per cursor page, and wait for full completion before corrections. Reviewers read live artifact paths and may inspect the codebase; coherent chunks and final consistency are mandatory. No retired protocol or self-review fallback.

name: insrc_schema
title: insrc schema (look up an insrc_* tool's input contract)
description:
Read-only: return the authoritative input contract (JSON Schema) for a specific insrc_* tool — for a multi-turn tool, the specific `phase` you are about to call. The schema is sliced from the tool's OWN registered shape, so it can never drift from what the tool enforces.

Call it BEFORE constructing a call whose shape you are unsure of, instead of guessing fields. Misses are structured, never thrown: omit / mistype `tool` to get { error, validTools }; omit / mistype `phase` on a multi-turn tool to get { error, validPhases }. A phaseless tool ignores a spurious `phase`.

tool.description: The insrc_* tool whose input contract you want (e.g. "insrc_workflow_step"). Omit it to receive the list of valid tools.

phase.description: For a multi-turn tool, the phase whose contract you want (e.g. "plan"). Ignored for a single-shape (phaseless) tool.

name: insrc_triage
title: insrc triage (classify size → route workflow entry)
description:
Classify a feature request by SIZE and route it to the right workflow start stage, so every feature — big or small — is tracked without the smallest ones drowning in ceremony. Call this FIRST when asked to build a feature, instead of hand-picking `define` / `design.story` / `build`.

Tiers: Epic → `define` (full chain); Feature → standalone `design.story` (LLD) → plan → build; Small → standalone `design.story` → build; Trivial → `build` (no LLD).

Two-turn loop:
  1. phase='start' with { focus, repo?, specHash? } (specHash: an approved SPEC to seed the routed stage). Server returns { next: 'emit_classification', prompt, schema, state }.
  2. GROUND the sizing on `insrc_analyze_step` passes (which modules/files it touches, caller counts, new-vs-reuse), emit a TriageResult JSON matching the schema, then phase='classify' with result=<your JSON> + state. Server returns { next: 'done', result, route, nextCall, summary } — `nextCall` is the exact pre-filled call to make next.

Preserve `state` verbatim between the two calls.

phase.description: Which turn of the loop this call carries.

focus.description: Only for phase=start. The feature request / scope statement to size.

repo.description: Only for phase=start. Absolute repo path; falls back to INSRC_REPO env.

specHash.description: Only for phase=start. The approved SPEC this request was brainstormed into. It must exist and be approved; it is forwarded into the routed design.story / define call so that stage is seeded from it.

result.description: Only for phase=classify. The TriageResult JSON your LLM emitted (matches the emit_classification schema).

state.description: Opaque continuation token from phase=start. Required for phase=classify.

name: insrc_workflow_approve
title: insrc workflow approve (in-CLI, controller-driven gate)
description:
Approve a workflow artifact WITHOUT leaving this session — the in-CLI approval gate. Call this ONLY after you have PRESENTED the artifact summary to the user and they have said yes in chat (the human still authorizes; this just executes it). Approve a SINGLE artifact with `artifactPath`, or a BATCH with `epicHash` (every review-clean, still-pending DEF/HLD/LLD/PLAN artifact under that epic). Exactly one of artifactPath | epicHash.

Approves the artifact in its lifecycle and ENFORCES the review rule: a DEF, HLD or LLD needs a review, and a BUILD record needs a code review of its Story, each done by the party that did NOT author the work; a blocking verdict also withholds. A withheld artifact comes back in `skipped[]` {path,reason}, never `approved[]` — relay both arrays to the user. An ISSUE, SPEC or PLAN needs no review. Approval only: it does NOT gh-push or commit (that stays with the TUI approve). Pass `overrideReview` to approve past a missing, same-party or blocking review with a recorded reason. `repo` falls back to the registered repo that contains the session workspace and is always sent to the daemon as an absolute path; the daemon refuses an approval whose repo is missing, not registered, or whose artifactPath is outside it. A relative `artifactPath` is taken relative to the repo.

artifactPath.description: Single-artifact target: the .md/.json artifact path to approve. Exactly one of artifactPath | epicHash.

epicHash.description: Batch target: approve every review-clean, still-pending artifact under this epic. Exactly one of artifactPath | epicHash.

repo.description: Absolute path of a registered repo; defaults to the registered repo that contains the session workspace. The daemon refuses a call whose repo is missing or not registered.

overrideReview.description: Optional review-override reason — approves past a HIGH/MED review block and records the reason on the artifact.

name: insrc_workflow_run
title: insrc workflow (async start/poll, daemon-driven)
description:
Run a full workflow SERVER-SIDE in the daemon, ASYNC. The daemon drives every phase (decompose → steps → synthesize → review) via its configured LLM provider; a long run no longer blocks this call.

Loop: START → POLL* → done.

  1. START — call with { workflow, focus, params?, repo? } (no poll/abort). Returns { runId, next:'poll', guidance } IMMEDIATELY; the run is now executing detached.
  2. POLL — call with { poll: <runId>, cursor: <n> } repeatedly (start cursor at 0). Each returns { status, progress:[short lines], cursor:<next> }. RELAY each `progress` batch to the user, then poll again with the returned cursor to get only NEW frames. Space polls a few seconds apart.
  3. DONE — when status is 'done' the response also carries { artifact, runId, model, review? }; when 'error' it carries { error }; 'aborted' ends the loop. Stop polling on any terminal status.

ABORT — call with { abort: <runId> } to cancel a run mid-flight (returns { aborted:true, runId }); the daemon run is really aborted.

Use this for a hands-off run you watch by polling. Use insrc_workflow_step instead when YOU want to drive each turn.

`repo` is the absolute path of a registered repo (default: the registered repo that contains the session workspace, sent explicitly); the daemon refuses a run without one.

workflow.description: START only. Which workflow to run (define / design.epic / design.story / plan / …).

focus.description: START only. Natural-language framing of the ask.

repo.description: START only. Absolute path of a registered repo; defaults to the registered repo that contains the session workspace. The daemon refuses a run whose repo is missing or not registered.

poll.description: POLL. A runId returned by a prior start call; fetches new progress + status.

cursor.description: POLL. Cursor from the previous poll (start at 0); returns only frames after it.

abort.description: ABORT. A runId to cancel mid-run.

name: insrc_workflow_step
title: insrc workflow (multi-turn)
description:
Phase-driven multi-turn workflow runner. Supports:

  - `define`        — Epic + Stories with citations (Phase B)
  - `design.epic`   — HLD: framework + shared contracts + rollout (Phase C)
  - `design.story`  — LLD: Story contract + tests + optional migration (Phase D)
  - `tracker.push`  — push Epic+Stories to GitHub Issues (Phase F)
  - `tracker.sync`  — pull GitHub Issue status back into artifact meta
  - `tracker.post`  — post HLD/LLD/amendment summary as issue comment
  - `stub`          — Phase A test workflow (echo/echo/echo)

Chain: define → design.epic → design.story (per Story) → tracker.*.
Each gate requires human approval via `insrc workflow approve <path>`.
Amendments to the HLD are typed proposals from downstream steps; review with `insrc workflow amend <slug> --list`. Use `insrc workflow chain <slug>` at any time to see status + the exact next command.

Multi-turn loop:

  1. phase='start' with { workflow, focus, params? }. Server returns
     { next: 'emit_plan', prompt, schema, state }.
  2. Emit the plan JSON matching the schema, then phase='plan'
     with plan=<your JSON> + state.
  3. If the server returns { next: 'emit_step', stepId, prompt,
     schema, state }, emit the JSON matching the schema and call
     phase='step' with stepId + response + state. Repeat until
     you receive emit_synthesize.
  4. Server returns { next: 'emit_synthesize', prompt, schema, state }.
     Emit the artifact JSON, then phase='synthesize' with artifact + state.
  5. Server returns { next: 'done', path, markdown, artifact } once
     the artifact has been written to disk. `done` may also carry
     `openQuestions` — the new artifact's own still-open questions;
     you MAY resolve them now via phase='resolve_question' (optional).

Open-question gate (design.epic / design.story / plan):
  - phase='start' first checks the IMMEDIATE-UPSTREAM artifact
    (design.epic->DEF, design.story->HLD, plan->LLD) for unresolved
    open questions. If any it returns { next: 'resolve_questions',
    questions: [{ questionId, text, options, recommendation }] } INSTEAD
    of emit_plan. Present each ONE AT A TIME (Resolve / Defer / Ignore),
    then call phase='resolve_question' with { workflow, params,
    questionId, choice? | defer? | ignore?, rationale? }. When it returns
    { next: 'ready' }, re-call phase='start'. Deferred questions do NOT
    re-trigger; surface them later with phase='review_deferred'
    { params: { epicHash | epicSlug } } -> { next: 'deferred', questions }.

Handing a stage over (team repos): phase='park' { epicHash, storyId?, runToken? } commits the
  unit's drafts and a checkpoint of the run to its handoff branch -> { next: 'parked', branch }.
  phase='resume' { epicHash, storyId?, workflow? } on the next owner's clone restores them and returns
  the turn the run stopped at (emit_plan / emit_step / emit_synthesize), or { next: 'restart' } to start
  the stage afresh. A unit another user holds is refused with team-gate-refused.

Common params:
  - design.epic:  { epicSlug }
  - design.story: { epicSlug, storyId }
  - tracker.push: { epicSlug, force? }
  - tracker.sync: { epicSlug }
  - tracker.post: { epicSlug, target: { kind: hld|lld|amendment, storyId?, amendmentId? } }

The `guidance` field on each response explains what to do next in one sentence; the `prompt` + `schema` fields are the authoritative instructions. Preserve `state` verbatim between calls.

phase.description: Which turn of the loop this call carries.

workflow.description: For phase=start (which workflow to run), phase=resolve_question (the consuming stage whose upstream artifact to patch) and phase=resume (the stage's workflow, only when it cannot be told from the committed artifacts).

focus.description: Only for phase=start. Natural-language framing of the ask.

repo.description: For phase=start / park / resume. Absolute path of a registered repo; for the first phase it defaults to the registered repo that contains the session workspace and is sent to the daemon explicitly. The daemon refuses a phase that writes files when the repo is missing or not registered; a later phase takes the repo of its run.

epicHash.description: Only for phase=park / resume. The Epic's hash.

storyId.description: Only for phase=park / resume. The Story to hand over (lowercase, e.g. s1); omit for the Epic itself.

runToken.description: Only for phase=park. The state token of the run to park; omitted, the run you own for the unit is found.

params.description: For phase=start / resolve_question / review_deferred. Workflow-specific params (epicHash, epicSlug, storyId, …).

questionId.description: Only for phase=resolve_question. The questionId from a prior resolve_questions / done.openQuestions response.

choice.description: Only for phase=resolve_question. The chosen option label/decision (omit when deferring/ignoring).

defer.description: Only for phase=resolve_question. Set true to defer this question to the review flow (does not re-trigger at stage boundaries).

ignore.description: Only for phase=resolve_question. Set true to leave this question to downstream judgment.

rationale.description: Only for phase=resolve_question. Optional one-line rationale for the choice / defer / ignore.

plan.description: Only for phase=plan. The WorkflowPlan JSON your LLM emitted.

stepId.description: Only for phase=step. Echo the stepId from the prior emit_step response.

response.description: Only for phase=step. The JSON your LLM emitted matching the emit_step schema.

artifact.description: Only for phase=synthesize. The artifact JSON matching the emit_synthesize schema.

state.description: Opaque continuation token from the prior response. Required after phase=start.
